# EU AI Act Reference

## Key Articles

### Art. 5 — Prohibited AI practices
AI systems that use subliminal manipulation, exploit vulnerabilities, social scoring by public authorities, or real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces are prohibited. Compliance tooling MUST NOT scaffold these capabilities.

### Art. 9 — Risk management
High-risk AI systems must implement a continuous risk management process: identify risks, evaluate likelihood and severity, adopt risk mitigation measures.

### Art. 10 — Data governance
Training, validation, and test data must meet quality criteria. Data practices must address biases. Personal data handling must comply with GDPR.

### Art. 13 — Transparency (model cards)
High-risk AI systems must provide information enabling users to understand capabilities, limitations, performance on relevant populations, known biases, and intended purpose.

### Art. 14 — Human oversight
High-risk AI systems must be designed so natural persons can effectively oversee the system during use. Oversight must be able to intervene or halt. Systems must allow humans to decide NOT to use AI output.

### Art. 62 — Serious incident reporting
Providers of high-risk AI in the EU must report serious incidents or malfunctioning to the relevant national supervisory authority within defined timeframes:
- Death or serious injury: 15 days
- Fundamental rights violation: 15 days
- Other serious incidents: 30 days

### Art. 86 — Right to explanation
Affected persons in high-risk AI decisions have the right to obtain a meaningful explanation of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main parameters affecting the output.

## Hard Gate

**NEVER claim EU AI Act compliance certification — that requires a qualified notified body (Art. 43).**
**NEVER cite article numbers not listed in this skill without noting they are from training data and may have been updated.**
